messages:
maria_sales: Heads-up — ACME POC is failing when they try to stream zipped docs to our /v1/generate endpoint. Demo tomorrow and they hit a 413 + truncated output. Any quick ideas?

aj_solution: Are they sending multipart/form-data or a raw binary body? Can you paste the exact request/response?

maria_sales: Paste from their QA environment:
```bash
curl -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/zip" 
  --data-binary @archive.zip 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
They also tried a presigned PUT flow but said the PUT times out for files >20MB. Logs show nginx: "client intended to send too large body" and our API returns truncated context when it gets through.

devon_engineer: 2 quick diagnostics: 1) Is this on our hosted API or a Private deployment behind customer's gateway? 2) Are they base64-encoding the zip in a JSON payload? Base64 expands payload by ~33% which often pushes it over limits.

maria_sales: Hosted. They initially tried to base64 into JSON (which exploded size), then switched to raw zip body which still failed.

infra_bot: deploy-bot: recent proxy log snippet: 
```
2026-03-20T11:42:07Z proxy[nginx]: client intended to send too large body: 12582912 bytes, client: 10.2.3.4, server: api.redwood.example
```

sophia_acme: FWIW from our side: presign PUTs are flaky in our browser pipeline for big files — we see intermittent 504s from our edge gateway during the S3 handshake. Multipart upload helps but our frontend team hasn't plumbed multipart yet.

devon_engineer: Root causes and options: 
- If they're sending files directly to our API, our hosted ingress has an upper body limit (default ~15MB on hosted).
- Base64-in-JSON will push them over that even for modest zips.
- Browsers + single PUTs to S3 can time out on slow connections — multipart S3 upload avoids single huge PUT timeouts.

Workarounds: 
1) Recommend presigned S3 + S3 multipart (client uploads pieces, then we pull/ingest once complete). This avoids sending binary through our API.
2) If they must send via API, chunk the archive client-side (zip parts) and upload multiple requests, then server-side reassemble.
3) Extract text on client (or a lightweight extractor) and send only text/summary — that avoids binary entirely and reduces token usage.

Example note: base64 expansion: 
```
archive.zip size = 12 MB -> base64 in JSON ≈ 16 MB -> plus JSON overhead -> hits 413
```

aj_solution: Also callout: model context limits are separate — even if you get binary through, once we extract text the tokenized context can exceed model context and get truncated. Recommend chunk+embed pattern (store chunks in vector DB, send relevant chunks).

maria_sales: Customer asks about the cost implication: if we tell them to use Dedicated to remove ingress limits, what's a ballpark? They expect ~10–50 POCs/month, avg 50MB per POC.

aj_solution: I'll pull numbers from pricing. Short answer: Dedicated removes shared-hosting body limits and gives predictable throughput, but ingress/egress still billed. For that volume, presigned S3 + hosted inference is usually cheaper than Dedicated unless they need guaranteed low-latency or private networks. I'll DM finance for a tailored quote.

devon_engineer: Immediate short-term fix for tomorrow's demo: 
- Ask ACME to do a quick multipart upload to their S3 (or a public S3 we control) and share a presigned URL for a single doc they care about. We can run the demo against that smaller sample.
- I'll also open an internal ops ticket to evaluate bumping the proxy max_body_size for their org if we sign them. If they go enterprise we can adjust ingress policies behind a contract.

maria_sales: Perfect. Can someone add a short troubleshooting note I can hand to their engineer? Simple steps they can try now.

aj_solution: Copy for handoff: 
1) Avoid base64-in-JSON for large zips. Use presigned S3 or multipart.
2) If using presign, prefer S3 multipart PUT for >15–20MB files.
3) If you must call /v1/generate with payload, chunk client-side (<10MB parts) and reassemble server-side.
4) Prefer text-extraction + chunk+embed to send only relevant context to the model.
5) If you need us to relax ingress limits, we'll need an enterprise contract and ops sign-off.

sophia_acme: Thanks — we'll try multipart S3 today and report back. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: created internal ticket INF-8245 to review per-customer proxy limits and presign stability.

maria_sales: Awesome, thanks everyone. I'll try the multipart presign demo path and loop back here before the call. :eyes:
